policy.headline: One more update this week, a stability release. Serious fixes still ship when they're needed.
points: Version 1.4 (a stability release) is planned for this week.

After 1.4, the next planned update is 1.4.1 (Clipy can edit and complete things you already have). Its date will be posted here. If a serious problem turns up before then, especially anything that could lose your data, a fix is still released as quickly as possible.
If an update isn't ready or hasn't been tested properly, it moves instead of shipping. This page says so and why.
The browser version (the website) updates as soon as a release is published, and shows a bar when a newer version is ready. The browser zip is attached to every release.

Windows and Linux can now update by themselves (version 1.3.2 and newer). In Control Panel you choose: install automatically, ask me first, or just tell me. If you're on 1.3.1 or older, install 1.3.2 by hand once. On a Mac the app tells you when an update is out and links to the download, because Apple's signing isn't paid for yet.
Windows is tested on a real PC. Linux can only be tested in a virtual environment.
notified: Press Watch on the GitHub page, then Custom, then Releases, to get an email for each release.
Add the releases feed to your feed reader.
In the desktop app, Control Panel shows when it last checked for updates and what it found.

upcoming.title: Stability release
items: No new features. Two security fixes in how notes are shown, a safer graphing calculator, and web lookups that can't reach your own network
Changes in two browser tabs now merge instead of overwriting each other
One app having a problem can't stop other windows updating
Quicker start-up, easier-to-read text, a Jump to row in Control Panel, and counts that read properly
Automatic safety checks now run in every build
upcoming.note: This is the first update that Windows and Linux copies of 1.3.2 can install by themselves.

upcoming.title: Clipy edits and completes things
items: Clipy can change or complete things you already have, like "move my study group to Saturday" or "mark the lab report done"

released.summary: Windows and Linux can update by themselves (you choose: automatic, ask first, or just tell me), Windows Now Playing checks every media session, Clipy has an Undo button and can make flash cards, pop-outs remember their size and position, the website shows a new-version bar, and the browser warns when storage is nearly full.

Clipy can add events, reminders, tasks and assignments when you ask (with an optional switch to write them to Apple Calendar), tidier pop-outs and a File > Pop Out App menu, no more back-to-back Clipy tips, and an accurate storage bar in the browser.
Write to Apple Calendar and Reminders (Mac), pop-out windows for apps, Apple's on-device model for M.X.E.S., optional Now Playing cover lookup, and loading your desktop backup in the browser.
Important fix: saved data wasn't read after updating if you had folders or structured citations.
Windows fixes: full screen, tougher saving, an optional taskbar number, a taskbar menu, and troubleshooting buttons.
Command palette, tags and courses, folders as course hubs, shortcuts you can change, and a better update checker.
Citation Maker 2.0, Sketch Pad 2.0, a flash-card hotkey, and Now Playing in the taskbar clock.
Apple Calendar and Reminders (reading), Periodic Table 2.0, and a calendar in the taskbar clock.
